subject: [PATCH v2 0/5] btrfs: handle -ENOMEM errors in some synchronous dirops without aborting

reviews.author: Qu Wenruo
reviews.summary: Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested simplifying the code by directly returning a btrfs_dir_index_prealloc pointer, reducing the parameter list.
reviews.raw_body:
We can directly return a btrfs_dir_index_prealloc pointer, which reduce 
the parameter list.

Otherwise looks good to me.

Reviewed-by: Qu Wenruo <wqu@suse.com>

Thanks,
Qu

reviews.author: Qu Wenruo
reviews.summary: Reviewer Qu Wenruo approved the patch, providing a Reviewed-by tag.

reviews.author: Qu Wenruo
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that when a pre-allocated path is passed in and an earlier allocation fails, the function returns -ENOMEM without freeing the pre-allocated path, resulting in a memory leak.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested merging the memcpy operation into the preallocation function, citing that the preallocation itself doesn't utilize the name->name field.
reviews.raw_body:
This is exposed by sashiko.

If we have @prealloc passed in, and before we even hit 
insert_with_overflow(), the previous btrfs_alloc_path() failed, we 
return -ENOMEM directly, leaking the @prealloc.

---

Sashiko also pointed out that, the preallocation itself doesn't really 
utilize name->name.

Thus it may be a good idea to merge the later memcpy() into the 
preallocation function.

Thanks,
Qu

2026-08-05.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a long-standing issue in the Btrfs file system where memory allocation failures can cause the file system to abort. The patches rework the code to perform memory allocations before critical points, preventing aborts due to ENOMEM errors. This includes changes to directory morphing and orphan handling, with additional tests added to exercise the new behavior. While not all potential cases are covered, this series is designed to work in conjunction with other patches to address remaining issues.
